profile.campus: Csquare Silicon Valley campus cluster (SFO1-SFO4, formerly Centersquare, formerly Evoque Data Center Solutions)
profile.address: 4650/4700 Old Ironsides Drive, Santa Clara, CA
profile.reading: This building is the second of two structures making up SFO2, part of Csquare Silicon Valley campus cluster at 4650 and 4700 Old Ironsides Drive in Santa Clara, California, mapped as a separate OpenStreetMap way from its immediate neighbor. Csquare, Inc., trading on the New York Stock Exchange as CSQR, is the current name of a data center real estate company whose Silicon Valley facilities trace back to CenturyLink Savvis-heritage colocation assets, divested and rebranded Evoque Data Center Solutions around 2020 to 2021 under Brookfield-affiliated ownership, later Centersquare, and now Csquare ahead of its July 16, 2026 initial public offering. That IPO priced at 21 dollars per share across 50 million shares for roughly 1.05 billion dollars gross, and Brookfield Corporation retained approximately 69 percent of voting power afterward, making Csquare a controlled company under NYSE rules. Per Csquare own SEC registration prospectus, the company overall portfolio as of March 31, 2026 spanned 64 sites across 21 major metro markets in the US, Canada, and the UK, totaling roughly 389 megawatts of sellable power capacity and more than 1,700 customers, with CEO Spencer Mullee and CFO Steven Cook both having joined from the company Evoque-era leadership. The same prospectus Properties table lists two Silicon Valley buildings under the SFO2 code, designated SFO2_A at 45,481 rentable square feet, 89.9 percent occupied, and SFO2_B at 56,289 rentable square feet, 94.9 percent occupied, both company-owned, though which specific street address corresponds to which suffix could not be confirmed this session, so no single building-level square footage figure is assigned to this record individually, and no tenant is named for either. Old Ironsides Drive sits within a dense corridor of Santa Clara colocation and enterprise data center buildings developed originally in the 1990s and 2000s telecom boom era, consistent with this campus CenturyLink Savvis-heritage origins described above.

reading.body:
Csquare SFO2 occupies 100,056 square feet across two adjacent buildings in Santa Clara's Old Ironsides corridor, a 1990s-2000s telecom-heritage area now repurposed for enterprise colocation. The operator publishes 43.2 MW of utility power and 14.1 MW of UPS capacity but does not label either as IT load; the distinction matters because utility power typically includes non-critical systems. The campus holds SOC 2 Type II, PCI-DSS, and NIST 800-53 PE High certifications, qualifying it for regulated workloads and government contracts. Neither the operator's spec sheet nor SEC filings name individual tenants.

The published figures do not support inference of current AI capacity. At 40 kW per rack, the 14.1 MW UPS figure would imply roughly 350 racks, but UPS capacity is designed for finite runtime, not sustained load, and this site's spec sheet does not separate legacy colocation from new AI-density deployments. Csquare as a company portfolio spans 64 sites totaling 389 MW; SFO2's 43.2 MW utility power ranks it twelfth by published MW within California's 103 mapped facilities, but California's published total is 365 MW across only 11 facilities with any disclosed figure, making state-level rankings volatile and dominated by a small set of disclosed campuses.

Whether this campus matters to AI scaling depends on utilization and power delivery to compute. Csquare went public in July 2026 and is controlled by Brookfield Corporation. The operator publishes utility power and UPS capacity but not critical load or accelerator count. No data published here indicates whether SFO2 is repurposed for AI training density or remains general-purpose colocation. The 22.5 MW of standby generation capacity is published but standby generation does not contribute to the grid constraint that binds AI scaling.
